description: Formal critique of Sabhlok et al. (2024) dust/thermal model showing underdetermination

references.thermal_model: Heat transfer simulation with dust-coated reflectors

key_finding.conclusion: Thermal mechanism CANNOT explain observed signal

dust_estimate_variation.conclusion: Dust estimate varies 20-80% with unconstrained parameters

model_underdetermination.description: Model has more free parameters than observational constraints
model_underdetermination.conclusion: Model is underdetermined - cannot reliably infer dust coverage

sabhlok_argument: 1. Observe link budget shortfall (15-20× lower than expected)
2. Assume dust causes both absorption AND thermal lensing
3. Numerically simulate heat transfer with dust parameter
4. Fit eclipse data to find dust coverage ~50%

logical_fallacy.name: Affirming the consequent
logical_fallacy.structure: If dust, then signal loss. Signal loss, therefore dust.
logical_fallacy.valid_form: If dust, then signal loss. Dust observed, therefore signal loss expected.

tep_structure: 4. Test: Perihelion η = -2.8082e-04, aphelion subset non-significant; 1.42σ cosD-only differential (Step 022)
5. Confirm: TEP gravitational signal explains anomaly
alternative_explanation.superiority: Makes independent predictions, testable, no free parameters from fitting

conclusion.verdict: Even in BEST CASE, thermal expansion << observed signal
conclusion.robustness: 8.6× mismatch is robust across all physically reasonable parameters

assessment.tep_alternative: Makes independent predictions, no free parameters from fitting
assessment.verdict: Sabhlok dust attribution unreliable; TEP provides superior explanation
